{{Short description|Axiom in set theory}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[Class (set theory)|class theories]], the '''axiom of global choice''' is a stronger variant of the [[axiom of choice]] that applies to [[proper classes]] of [[Set (mathematics)|sets]] as well as sets of sets. Informally it states that one can simultaneously choose an element from every [[Empty set|non-empty]] set.

== Statement ==

The axiom of global choice states that there is a [[Choice function#Bourbaki tau function|global choice function]] τ, meaning a function such that for every non-empty set ''z'', τ(''z'') is an element of ''z''.

The axiom of global choice cannot be stated directly in the language of [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]] (ZF) with the [[axiom of choice]] (AC), known as ZFC, as the choice function τ is a proper class and in ZFC one cannot quantify over classes. It can be stated by adding a new function symbol τ to the language of ZFC, with the property that τ is a global choice function. This is a [[conservative extension]] of ZFC: every provable statement of this extended theory that can be stated in the language of ZFC is already provable in ZFC {{harv|Fraenkel|Bar-Hillel|Levy|1973|loc=p.72}}.  Alternatively, [[Kurt Gödel|Gödel]] showed that given the [[axiom of constructibility]] one can write down an explicit (though somewhat complicated) choice function τ in the language of ZFC, so in some sense the axiom of constructibility implies global choice (in fact, [ZFC proves that] in the language extended by the unary function symbol τ, the axiom of constructibility implies that if τ is said explicitly definable function, then this τ is a global choice function. And then global choice morally holds, with τ as a [[Witness (mathematics)|witness]]).

In the language of [[von Neumann–Bernays–Gödel set theory]] (NBG) and [[Morse–Kelley set theory]], the axiom of global choice can be stated directly {{harv|Fraenkel|Bar-Hillel|Levy|1973|loc=p.133}}, and is equivalent to various other statements:

* Every class of nonempty sets has a [[choice function]].
* '''V''' \ {∅} has a choice function (where '''V''' is the [[von Neumann universe|class of all sets]]).
* There is a [[well-ordering]] of '''V'''.
* There is a [[bijection]] between '''V''' and the class of all [[ordinal number]]s.

In von Neumann–Bernays–Gödel set theory, global choice does not add any consequence about ''sets'' (not proper classes) beyond what could have been deduced from the ordinary axiom of choice.

Global choice is a consequence of the [[axiom of limitation of size]].
